questions.prompt: Put the phases of heap sort in order.
steps: Build a max-heap from the array, starting at the last non-leaf node and moving up
Swap the root (the current maximum) with the last element of the heap
Shrink the heap by one so the moved maximum stays in its sorted place
Heapify from the root to restore the max-heap on the remaining elements
Repeat the swap, shrink and heapify until one element is left
questions.explanation: Heap sort first builds a max-heap, then repeatedly moves the root to the end of the unsorted part, shrinks the heap and re-heapifies.

questions.prompt: Why does the build-heap loop start at index `n / 2 - 1` and go backwards?
options: Because nodes after `n / 2 - 1` are leaves, which already satisfy the heap property, and going backward fixes child heaps before their parents
Because the second half of the array is already sorted
Because index `n / 2 - 1` always holds the largest value
Because `Heapify` can only move values towards the end of the array
questions.explanation: Leaves have no children, so they are already valid heaps. Working backward from the last non-leaf node ensures each subtree is a heap before its parent is processed.
The children of index 0 are at 1 (`5`) and 2 (`3`). `5` is the largest, so it swaps with the root; the recursive call on index 1 has no children within `n = 3`, so it stops.

questions.prompt: Heap sort and quicksort are both O(n log n) on average. Why is heap sort usually slower in practice?
options: It needs an O(n) auxiliary array
It has poor cache locality, because it jumps around the array via heap indices
It degrades to O(n²) on sorted input
It has to sort the array once before building the heap
questions.explanation: Heap sort has no bad worst case and uses O(1) extra space, but its jumps between parent and child indices give poor cache locality.

questions.prompt: When does the lesson recommend heap sort?
options: When equal elements must keep their original order
When the input is nearly sorted
When the values are small integers in a known range
When memory is tight but you still need guaranteed O(n log n) performance
questions.explanation: Heap sort's strength is guaranteed O(n log n) with O(1) extra space. It is not stable, so it is a poor fit when ties must keep their order.
